articles.title: Sabalenka gana a Muchova y Andreeva a Svitolina en las Finales WTA
articles.standfirst: Superaron a la checa Karolina Muchova y a la ucraniana Elena Svitolina, respectivamente
articles.summary: Superaron a la checa Karolina Muchova y a la ucraniana Elena Svitolina, respectivamente
articles.body: La bielorrusa Aryna Sabalenka y la rusa Mirra Andreeva superaron a la checa Karolina Muchova y a la ucraniana Elena Svitolina, respectivamente, en su debut en las Finales de la WTA en 2026 que se disputan en Indian Wells. Sabalenka, número dos del mundo, se deshizo de Muchova (n.7) por 7-6(2) y 7-5 en 1 hora y 53 minutos. La bielorrusa, que perdió el número uno en septiembre tras casi dos años, nunca ha ganado unas Finales de la WTA. Por su lado, Andreeva, vigente campeona en Roland Garros, derrotó a Svitolina por 6-4 y 6-0 en solo 1 hora y 10 minutos. Para Svitolina, este fue su primer partido desde que anunció su separación del francés Gael Monfils, su esposo. Andreeva y Sabalenka encabezan ahora el Grupo 2 de las Finales de la WTA, que reúne a las ocho mejores tenistas del año, a la conclusión de la primera jornada. Este martes arranca la segunda jornada con los partidos del Grupo 1 entre la estadounidense Coco Gauff y la checa Linda Noskova y entre la también estadounidense Jessica Pegula y la ucraniana Marta Kostyuk. Noskova y Gauff lideran ese grupo tras sus respectivas victorias del domingo ante Kostyuk y Pegula.

articles.title: Sinner: "El objetivo es volver en Australia, pero tengo que ir paso a paso"
articles.standfirst: El italiano concede una rueda de prensa en Milán y reconoce que "por primera vez en mi carrera, no tengo control sobre las cosas"
articles.summary: El italiano habla para La Gazzetta sobre su tratamiento en la rodilla,
articles.body: Jannik Sinner, apartado de las pistas desde el 12 de julio por una lesión en la rodilla derecha, ha concedido una rueda de prensa en Milán para tratar su situación actual con el tratamiento conservador y cómo es la vida fuera del circuito. También le ha acompañado su ya exentrenador, Darren Cahill, con el que anunció su separación profesional hace tan solo cuatro días y para el que siempre tiene buenas palabras: "Darren tiene mucha experiencia. Ha vivido momentos en la pista antes que yo y me ha ayudado mucho a lo largo de estos años". No son tiempos fáciles para Jannik, con cinco Masters 1000 y un grande a sus espaldas, tuvo que verse obligado a despedirse de la temporada para centrarse en su rodilla derecha: "No son meses fáciles, echo de menos la competición y dar el 100%. Si volviera a la pista un mes después, nada cambiaría. Quiero jugar otros 10 o 15 años más. Fue un año interesante. Gané Wimbledon y Roma, lo que me dio una alegría enorme, pero ahora tengo que centrarme en seguir los tratamientos", empieza el italiano. También ha mencionado la presión que siente por volver: "Siento un poco la presión, no puedo evitarlo. Teníamos un objetivo en mente, China, y tuvimos que cambiar las cosas sobre la marcha. Tengo que hacer caso a lo que me dicen los médicos". El transalpino ha querido marcar su gran objetivo: "El objetivo es volver en Australia. Quizás jugar algunos torneos antes, pero tengo que ir paso a paso hacia ese objetivo, porque si nos precipitamos, las cosas podrían empeorar. Pero el objetivo es Australia", aclara. Sobre si continúa viendo tenis aun estando fuera: "No veía mucho porque yo también quería estar allí. Antes, jugar un torneo y ganarlo me parecía lo más normal del mundo. Ahora que lo echo de menos, valoro aún más lo que he logrado. Seguiré viviendo el tenis de la misma manera, con amor y pasión, porque tengo la suerte de haberlo elegido como profesión", ha querido añadir el campeón de cinco grandes. Aunque los días, según cuenta, se le están haciendo largos al tenista de San Cándido: "Por primera vez en mi carrera, no tengo control sobre las cosas. Es un momento difícil porque voy del simulador al gimnasio y luego al simulador... Viajo un poco, visito a amigos y luego a mis padres. Así que estoy viviendo algo que nunca antes había experimentado. No tengo el control de la situación. Esta es quizás la parte más difícil de este período, pero solo tengo que ser paciente y confiar", cierra Jannik Sinner.

articles.title: Jannik Sinner: World No 2 confirms aim to return to tennis at Australian Open after lengthy absence with knee injury
articles.summary: Jannik Sinner has confirmed his plans to return from injury at the Australian Open in January; The World No 2 has not played since July and recently lost the top spot in the rankings to Alexander Zverev; watch the WTA Finals this week, live on Sky Sports Tennis
articles.body:
The Italian has not played since defending his Wimbledon title in July due to a knee injury.

Sinner, who has lost his world number one spot to Alexander Zverev, won the Melbourne title in 2024 and 2025 but was beaten by Novak Djokovic in this year's semi-final.

"The goal is to return to Australia," the 25-year-old said at press conference in Milan.

"Maybe play a few tournaments earlier. But I have to take everything one step after the other every day towards the goal because if we hurry then maybe it will be worse. But yes, the goal is Australia"

The five-time Grand Slam winner also lauded Brit Jack Draper alongside Matteo Berrettini and Carlos Alcaraz for his support during his period out with injury.

Draper himself has ruled out returning before 2027 after missing every Grand Slam this year, and said he was in a "difficult place" after his first-round defeat by Martin Landaluce in the Cincinnati Open in August, admitting he was struggling to escape the mental fatigue that had built up during 15 months of battling serious injury.

"When I announced that my season was over, Berrettini and Draper got in touch straight away," Sinner added. "Jack is also going through a difficult period, so he understands what I'm going through.

"Alcaraz had sent me a message, just as I message him. I really appreciated it.

"We are trying to find a way out of this situation and working towards experiencing those emotions again.

"For me, tennis is not a job. I continue to play because I enjoy it."

Alongside detailing his rehabilitation process, Sinner extended his congratulations to fellow Italian Kimi Antonelli after the 20-year-old became the youngest ever Formula 1 World Champion after finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix .

"Motorsport is the only sport I watch that gets me excited. When I watch MotoGP and Formula 1, it gives me an incredible boost.

"Kimi has done something incredible. He's learned so much this year, and what he's done moves me deeply.

"He's a completely normal, very laid-back guy, and this shows the most normal side of a 20-year-old, which is what we have most in common."

articles.title: La gesta de Pliskova: ganar 1.002 puestos tras 'reaprender' a caminar
articles.standfirst: La checa, que empezó la temporada como la 1.054 y la acabará entre las 60 primeras, protagoniza la mayor subida de posiciones en la WTA de la temporada 2026
articles.summary: La checa, que empezó la temporada como la 1.054 y la acabará entre las 60 primeras, protagoniza la mayor subida de posiciones en la WTA de la temporada 2026
articles.body: Karolina Pliskova, la que en 2017 fuera reina del circuito femenino, ha protagonizado la mayor subida de posiciones en el ranking WTA de la presente temporada. La checa comenzaba la semana del 5 de enero como la 1.054 en las listas. A día 10 de noviembre firma la posición 52, protagonizando un ascenso de 1.002 escalones. En el US Open 2024, mientras disputaba su partido de segunda ronda ante Jasmine Paolini, Pliskova sufrió una rotura de los ligamentos del tobillo izquierdo tras una caída en el tercer punto del encuentro. Siempre alardeaba de su capacidad para jugar a pesar del dolor y que nunca se retiraría de un partido, a no ser que la situación fuera realmente grave. Aquella vez, lo era. "Se te olvida cómo caminar, pierdes toda la musculatura, toda la movilidad. Y el tobillo es un problema porque todo el cuerpo recae sobre él. Tienes que empezar a usarlo de nuevo poco a poco", declaraba Pliskova durante el pasado mes de junio en el torneo de Queens. La bota ortopédica que llegó a portar por seis meses no le permitía ni pisar el suelo. Se complicó aún más cuando tuvo que volver a pasar por el quirófano tras una infección en la zona, lo que la obligó a estar dos meses más sin apoyar. Un año de sufrimiento e incertidumbre. Por aquel entonces, la que era 44 del mundo, pasó a ser la 1.056. En el presente curso, la checa ha demostrado que vuelve a ser competitiva. Los cuartos de final alcanzados en Madrid o las semifinales en Nottingham han ayudado a la gran subida de la campeona de 17 títulos WTA. Más de 1.000 posiciones después, se encuentra entre las 60 mejores raquetas femeninas (52), justo donde la lesión la obligó a parar hace dos años.

articles.title: Jannik Sinner targets late-December comeback, keeps Australian Open 2027 in focus
articles.summary: Jannik Sinner is targeting a return to competitive tennis in late December as he steps up his recovery from a persistent knee injury, with the Six Kings
articles.body: Jannik Sinner is targeting a return to competitive tennis in late December as he steps up his recovery from a persistent knee injury, with the Six Kings Slam in Saudi Arabia emerging as a possible first stop ahead of the 2027 Australian Open.The Italian, who has been sidelined since winning the Wimbledon title in July, offered an update on his recovery at a event in Milan on Tuesday. While he is keen to return to the court before the new season, Sinner made it clear that he will not rush the process at the risk of aggravating his injury."The aim is to go to Australia, the aim is also maybe to do a couple of tournaments first. But I have to respect the protocols at the moment because if we rush things we could have more serious problems," Sinner said."I also only have that information, that I have to work hard every day for that objective and then we'll see."Six Kings Slam could mark Sinner's returnThe rescheduled Six Kings Slam in Riyadh is among the events Sinner is targeting as he looks to regain match fitness before the Australian Open. The exhibition tournament, which was initially scheduled for October, has been moved to December 27-30 amid security concerns in the Middle East. Sinner acknowledged that the event remains a possibility rather than a certainty, with the wider situation in the region also playing a part in the decision."That (is the target) but we all know the situation what's there at the moment, which is not the best, so this is not our decision as players, this is a more general decision," he said.The Italian added that playing some matches before travelling to Australia could be beneficial, given that he has not competed since Wimbledon."But I think if we want to prepare for Australia (and) I'm not playing since Wimbledon, some matches before might be very helpful," he added.The Six Kings Slam does not offer ATP ranking points but brings together some of the biggest names in men's tennis. Sinner won the previous edition and is expected to feature alongside Carlos Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic, Alexander Zverev, Taylor Fritz and Alex de Minaur.Knee injury ended Sinner's 2026 season earlySinner's last appearance came in the Wimbledon final in July, where he defeated Alexander Zverev to claim the fifth Grand Slam title of his career. However, a right knee problem subsequently forced him to miss several tournaments, including the US Open.The prolonged recovery eventually led the 25-year-old to announce in October that he would not compete again in the 2026 ATP season. His extended absence also saw him lose the world No. 1 ranking, with Zverev taking over the top spot last week after Sinner's 95-week reign.Sinner has reiterated that his priority is to return fully fit rather than risk a setback by making an early comeback. With the Australian Open scheduled for January, the late-December target could offer him an opportunity to get valuable match practice before the first Grand Slam of 2027.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “Choose wisely”: Andre Agassi opens up on finding lasting love with Steffi Graf after going through a failed marriage
articles.summary: Andre Agassi, the tennis legend, has been public about the traumatic and painful childhood he went through as his father trained him intensely.
articles.body: Andre Agassi, the tennis legend, has been public about the traumatic and painful childhood he went through as his father trained him intensely. While that has been a dark chapter in Andre Agassi’s career, one thing he has always taken pride in is his high profile marriage to fellow tennis champion, Steffi Graf. After over two decades of being together, Andre Agassi opens up on choosing a life partner.Andre Agassi reflects on what's important in marriage as his bond with Steffi Graf inspires millionsIn an interview with E! News, the tennis legend Andre Agassi reflected on the secret behind a long lasting and happy marriage as he joked, "Choose wisely," before adding, "No, I mean, I think it's like success in life or in anything you do. I think there's a determination you have to be in the most of yourself, in balance of the most of what somebody needs from you, giving what it is you have to give and not attempting to give what you don't.”Andre Agassi added, “But not leaving anything in the tank when you can give it right."The tennis legend also reflected on how he and Steffi Graf have remained best friends for over two decades as he continued, "We love cooking together," Andre added. "We love hiking together. We love even grocery shopping together, dividing and conquering. So it's real life. And we're blessed."In the last two decades, Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf have quickly turned into one of the most inspiring couples. Both of them have remained pretty protective about their two children, Jaden, 22, and Jaz, 20, as they have publicly spoken of how there is no pressure on them to choose a career in tennis or professional sports.However, life was not always this perfect for Andre Agassi. Before he met and fell in love with Steffi Graf, he was married to popular actress Brooke Shields.Andre Agassi experienced a painful divorce before he fell for Steffi GrafWhile Andre Agassi and Brooke Shields dared each other for a few years before tying the knot, things did not work out well between them.With Andre Agassi’s busy career, the two hardly found any time to spend together and this created a lot of emotional distance between them. To make it worse, there had also been many infidelity rumors surrounding their high profile marriage.Just two years after tying the knot, Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf went their separate ways in 1999.Two years later, Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf tied the knot in 2001 and the rest was history. articles.title: Aryna Sabalenka controversy: beIN SPORTS apologises after commentator's shocking on-air remark goes viral
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka found herself at the centre of an uncomfortable controversy at the WTA Finals, but this time, the attention had little to do with her
articles.body: Aryna Sabalenka found herself at the centre of an uncomfortable controversy at the WTA Finals, but this time, the attention had little to do with her tennis. A comment about the Belarusian star's appearance was accidentally picked up during a live broadcast, leaving viewers stunned. The clip quickly circulated online, prompting criticism of the broadcaster. As the backlash grew, beIN SPORTS France issued a public apology, with a senior executive condemning the remark and distancing the network from the incident.Aryna Sabalenka faces appearance controversy as beIN SPORTS issues apologyThe incident unfolded during Sabalenka's player introduction at the WTA Finals. As the camera focused on the World No. 2, an off-air conversation became audible to viewers watching the coverage.A commentator could be heard saying, “Look, look… she looks horrible.”The remark immediately attracted criticism after a clip surfaced on the tennis account Tiempo De Tenis. Another account, L’Arene, shared the footage and directly tagged beIN SPORTS France, demanding a response over the comment.Viewers questioned why a professional athlete's appearance had become a subject of discussion during an important tournament broadcast. The controversy soon reached the broadcaster's management.Florent Houzot, beIN SPORTS France's Director of Broadcast Operations, Programming, and Editorial, addressed the situation publicly. He expressed regret and strongly criticised the comments made during the coverage.“I regret and strongly condemn the remarks made live on air this evening during the WTA Finals broadcast,” Houzot said.He also stressed that the comments did not reflect the broadcaster's values and reaffirmed its commitment to respecting athletes and everyone involved in sports coverage.However, the identity of the commentator and any possible disciplinary action remain unconfirmed.The situation has drawn comparisons with another tennis broadcasting controversy from November 2024. Tennis Channel commentator Jon Wertheim faced criticism after making remarks about Barbora Krejcikova's forehead during WTA Finals coverage in Riyadh.Wertheim later apologised, while Tennis Channel removed him from its broadcasts indefinitely. The network also issued an apology to Krejcikova.There is no confirmation that beIN SPORTS will take similar action in Sabalenka's case.Aryna Sabalenka defeats Karolina Muchova despite difficult WTA Finals startAway from the controversy, Sabalenka had business to handle on court. The two-time Grand Slam champion opened her WTA Finals campaign with a 7-6(2), 7-5 victory over Karolina Muchova.It was far from an easy evening. Muchova broke Sabalenka early and even served for the opening set. However, the Belarusian recovered and dominated the tiebreak.The second set brought another challenge, with both players exchanging breaks before Sabalenka finally secured the victory.Her serve also caused problems. She recorded seven double faults and four aces, landing only 59% of her first serves.Explaining the difficult conditions, Sabalenka said, “It was a bit tricky with the sun [and] with the shade. Sometimes I had to adjust my toss, sometimes I had to serve blind, but it’s all part of the game,” Sabalenka said.The win gave her a positive start in her sixth consecutive WTA Finals appearance. Having finished runner-up in 2022 and 2025, Sabalenka remains determined to capture her first title at the season-ending tournament.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: WTA Finals: Linda Noskova beats Coco Gauff to reach semi-finals, Jessica Pegula wins
articles.summary: Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova dismantles Coco Gauff to become the first player to reach the last four at the WTA Finals.
articles.body:
Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova dismantled Coco Gauff to become the first player to reach the last four of the WTA Finals.

Czech Noskova played with controlled aggression and served brilliantly to beat the American 6-3 6-3.

World number eight Noskova was composed throughout and broke Gauff's serve four times in the first set alone.

She sent powerful winners to all corners to outmuscle her opponent, who is one of the best movers on the WTA Tour, and committed only one unforced error in a dominant second set.

The 21-year-old fittingly sealed victory with an ace to secure a place in the semi-finals on her tournament debut.

"Thank you guys for the cheers I'm getting now - but it was a little weaker in the match, guys, I'm not going to lie," Noskova joked to the California crowd afterwards.

"I feel like I stayed in the match through every moment, from beginning to end."

It is a sixth top-10 victory of the season for Noskova, who won her maiden Grand Slam at Wimbledon in July.

Gauff, who won a thriller against compatriot Jessica Pegula on Sunday, had a poor day on serve.

She hit the same amount of aces and double faults - eight apiece - and won only six of 24 points behind her second serve.

Fourth-ranked Gauff can still qualify for the last four, as can Pegula.

Earlier in group one, Pegula claimed her first win since September to eliminate alternate Marta Kostyuk.

American Pegula won 6-2 7-5 in a scrappy match that saw seven breaks of serve.

Ukraine's Kostyuk, who has been dealing with a wrist injury since August, only found out she would be playing on Saturday after world number one Elena Rybakina withdrew.

She lost her opener to Noskova on Sunday and struggled for rhythm and consistency in a low-quality match against Pegula.

Pegula made only five unforced errors to Kostyuk's 17 as she took the first set, and the home favourite quickly went up a break in the second.

However, four breaks of serve then ensued, with Pegula eventually sealing the decisive break at 5-5 before serving out victory.

Elsewhere, Britain's Toby Samuel fell 6-1 6-4 to world number 25 Lorenzo Musetti in the Basel Open second round.

articles.title: WTA Finals: Linda Noskova dismantles Coco Gauff to reach semi-finals as Jessica Pegula keeps hopes alive with victory
articles.summary: Linda Noskova first through to Indian Wells semi-finals; Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula both have one win; Noskova faces Pegula on Thursday, while Gauff takes on Marta Kostyuk; watch the WTA Finals this week, live on Sky Sports Tennis
articles.body:
It was a commanding display from the Czech against the world No 4, as Noskova made it two wins from two with another impressive performance following her victory over Marta Kostyuk.

The 21-year-old is yet to drop a set at the WTA Finals, underlining her excellent form as she continues to enjoy an outstanding season.

She has now advanced with her two wins, while Gauff and Jessica Pegula sit on one win and one loss in Group One.

After suffering two defeats, Kostyuk has been eliminated from the tournament. The Ukrainian replaced world No 1 Elena Rybakina, who was forced to withdraw due to illness.

Pegula, meanwhile, bounced back from her defeat to Gauff to keep her hopes of reaching the WTA Finals semi-finals alive with a 6-2 7-5 victory over Kostyuk.

Pegula made an explosive start, breaking the Ukrainian in the opening game before securing a second break to comfortably take the first set 6-2.

Kostyuk offered greater resistance in the second set, putting Pegula under more pressure, but the American struck with a crucial late break before serving out the match to seal a straight-sets victory.

articles.title: 2026 was the year of tennis star Alexandra Eala – and she brings a nation with her
articles.summary: Hues of royal blue, red, white, and yellow flashed at every corner of center court as the crowd rallied around Alexandra Eala.
articles.body: Hues of royal blue, red, white, and yellow flashed at every corner of the tennis court as the crowd rallied around Alexandra Eala. For a sport constantly looking for the next generational icon, Eala has become a unifying touchstone for an archipelagic nation of over 110 million people – with many of them scattered across the globe. The left-handed Filipina player had a whirlwind breakout season after defeating several top women’s stars. She ousted defending Wimbledon title holder Iga Świątek in the third round of the grass court major this summer. In August, she then beat Jessica Pegula in the Washington Open to become the first player from the Philippines to win a WTA Tour singles title. Eala started this year as world No. 53. She’s now ranked 15th, a career-high after she made the final at the Prudential Hong Kong Tennis Open in her last tournament of the season. The distinction means the 21-year-old is now the highest-ranked Filipino player and Southeast Asian in WTA history. The Filipino talent has already shown she can beat some of the sport’s biggest names, but with every new game, set and match on tour, it is inevitably harder to stay at the top. “I think that the expectation rises, but so does the demand in terms of what the sport demands of you and what the level demands of you,” Eala told CNN Sports. Though she very well may still be asking herself if she can be among the greatest in the sport, Eala knows she’s working towards that consistency and getting better. “I just look forward to having another season full of hardship, full of joy, and hopefully full of success,” she said with pensive confidence. Though her bid for another WTA title fell short in Hong Kong, the loss has done little to dim her breakout year. “This season has changed my life,” Eala told the crowd as tears welled up following her loss to Claire Liu in the Hong Kong Open final. “It has changed my life for the better. I am incredibly proud of the work we have put in this year. We are the only ones who truly knew what it took to arrive at this point in our journey.” Eala and Liu had found themselves locked in a fierce, early back-and-forth at Victoria Park in Hong Kong, but the 26-year-old American soon switched gears and took control – at one point winning nine consecutive games – to seal a 6-3, 6-0 victory in an hour and 33 minutes to claim her first-ever WTA title. “I can’t speak for everyone, but playing against Alex is one of the hardest things because of the crowd. No matter where she goes, she always has so many supporters, which I think is really great in general for tennis,” Liu said in a post-tournament presser. Beyond the breakthrough Wherever she played, Filipino fans have clamored for tickets to cheer Eala on, bringing a sense of home to a life spent traveling the global tennis circuit. Eala’s growing popularity has even seen her swing from the tennis court to haute couture. In September, the Filipino phenom sat front row alongside Anna Wintour at New York Fashion Week’s Michael Kors and Tory Burch shows. Tennis courts transform into homecoming celebrations when Eala makes an appearance. And it was no exception in Hong Kong, which is home to over 200,000 Filipinos, many of them who work as Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs). “We idolize her for her resilience, same as an OFWs who never give up,” Lids Romero, a domestic worker who spent her only day off on Sunday to watch the final at the official fan zone, told CNN Sports. Moy Volante, who flew in with his family from the Philippines to watch the tournament, told CNN Sports he admired Eala’s determination to push through, even in tough battles, which he hopes his daughter can embody. “You can really feel the unity and support of Filipinos,” Volante said of the atmosphere throughout the week. “I love their passion,” Eala said fondly of her fans. “They really support me without fail in so many tournaments.” Crowds of Filipino domestic workers, young professionals and school children all came out to Causeway Bay to watch Eala in action, even as her matches stretched late into the night over a regular school week. Young female fans were all over Victoria Park with some holding placards proclaiming, “Let’s Go! Alex” at the fan zone, while others in the stands waved colorful, hand-drawn banners. “I want them to get inspiration from Alex,” Marlon Avines who was at the park with his three daughters, said to CNN Sports. “The grit, persistence and giving pride to the country.” Eala has encouraged girls and young women who look up to her “to pursue whatever makes them happy.” “I think it’s better to go through the hardships doing what you love, and you can always come back to that when things get difficult,” Eala told CNN Sports. The young, rising star is no stranger to hardships. She began training in tennis as a preschooler, coached by her late grandfather, who she affectionately calls “Lolo Bob.” What started as a family pastime soon grew into a relentless pursuit, which Eala once described on Maria Sharapova’s podcast as an obsession like having a “crush on perfection.” In 2018, as a 12-year-old wild card, she won Les Petits As – a tournament widely considered to be the preeminent under-14 competition in the world – in the process becoming a talent to watch. A few months later – after turning 13 – she left Manila for Mallorca to train at the Rafa Nadal Academy in Spain on a scholarship. Eala began to flourish on the international junior circuit, winning her first junior grand slam title at the 2020 Australian Open in girls’ doubles. Just two years later, she became the first Filipina to lift a junior grand slam singles trophy at the US Open in 2022. Along with that junior success, she officially turned pro in March 2020. While Eala’s stature in the sport grows, what remains the same is the standard of discipline she sets for herself. “I’ve learned to push my limits,” Eala told CNN Sports. “I’ve learned a lot about what my limits are … and the bar can always be raised.”

articles.title: Noskova se clasifica para semifinales de las Finales WTA y Kostyuk cae eliminada
articles.standfirst: La estadounidense Jessica Pegula (n.5) se impuso a Kostyuk (n.9) por 6-2 y 7-5 en 1 hora y 28 minutos.
articles.summary: La estadounidense Jessica Pegula (n.5) se impuso a Kostyuk (n.9) por 6-2 y 7-5 en 1 hora y 28 minutos.
articles.body: La checa Linda Noskova se convirtió en la primera semifinalista de las Finales de la WTA tras derrotar a la estadounidense Coco Gauff, mientras que la ucraniana Marta Kostyuk cayó eliminada. Noskova, vigente campeona en Wimbledon y número 8 del mundo, ganó a Gauff (n.4) por 6-3 y 6-3 en 1 hora y 15 minutos. La checa, que derrotó a Kostyuk en su primer partido, se ha asegurado la clasificación a falta de una jornada. Por su lado, la estadounidense Jessica Pegula (n.5) se impuso a Kostyuk (n.9) por 6-2 y 7-5 en 1 hora y 28 minutos. La ucraniana, que ha perdido sus dos partidos, entró en el torneo en la víspera de su inicio para tomar el lugar de la número uno del mundo, la kazaja Elena Rybakina, baja por enfermedad. Pegula y Gauff se jugarán este jueves la segunda plaza del Grupo 1 para las semifinales, en sus respectivos partidos contra Noskova y Kostyuk. Las Finales de la WTA reúnen a las ocho mejores tenistas del año en Indian Wells (Estados Unidos).

articles.title: El sorteo condicionado de las ATP Finals de Turín: Alcaraz debutará con Jódar o Tiafoe
articles.standfirst: Los dos tenistas españoles tienen un 50 por ciento de posibilidades de cruzarse en el primer partido
articles.summary: Los dos tenistas españoles tienen un 50 por ciento de posibilidades de cruzarse en el primer partido
articles.body: Fue el pasado mes de enero, en la previa del Open de Australia, cuando Carlos Alcaraz y Rafa Jódar se citaron por primera vez para entrenar. Quien le iba a decir al joven madrileño, en ese momento el 165 del mundo, que iba a acompañar 10 meses después a su condecorado compatriota en las ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22). Alcaraz y Jódar estarán este jueves en el bombo del sorteo de la cita de maestros que se inicia este domingo. Como marca el sistema de competición, según ha podido saber MARCA, los emparejamientos del primer partido están condicionados por el ranking de los participantes. Alexander Zverev y Carlitos, los dos primeros cabezas de serie, sólo pueden cruzarse en el debut con Frances Tiafoe o Jódar, séptimo y octavo en clasificarse para el certamen. De esta forma, hay un 50 por ciento de posibilidades de que Carlitos, flamante campeón de Viena y París, se mida a Rafa en el estreno. El rival del de Leganés sólo puede ser el murciano o Zverev, por lo que tendrá una puesta de largo por todo lo alto en el Masters que reúne al 'top8' de 2026. Ben Shelton y Daniil Medvedev, tercero y cuarto, se cruzarán en el primer partido ante Flavio Cobolli o Arthur Fils, quinto y sexto. Tiafoe y Jódar son dos de los cuatro debutantes en las ATP Finals. .Los otros dos son Cobolli y Fils. El italiano Jannik Sinner, campeón las dos últimas ediciones, es la sensible ausencia por la lesión en su rodilla derecha que arrastra desde el pasado verano.

articles.title: Otro micro abierto sacude de nuevo el mundo del tenis: "Sabalenka es horrible..."
articles.standfirst: Un micrófono abierto captó el comentario del periodista Matthieu Solier sobre la apariencia física de Sabalenka
articles.summary: Un micrófono abierto captó el comentario del periodista Matthieu Solier sobre la apariencia física de Sabalenka
articles.body: Aryna Sabalenka fue descrita como "horrible" por un periodista, en un vergonzoso incidente provocado por un micrófono que quedó abierto. La tenista de 28 años posaba y lanzaba un beso a la cámara durante la grabación de un vídeo promocional para las WTA Finals que realizaba beIN Sports en Indian Wells, California. De fondo se pudo escuchar al periodista Matthieu Solier decir de fondo: "Mira, mira, mira, es horrible (su aspecto)", sin darse cuenta de que su insulto estaba siendo retransmitido ante una gran audiencia. Un usuario de X compartió rápidamente el vídeo y lo calificó de "vergonzoso", lo que provocó una respuesta de Florent Houzot, directivo de beIN Sports. "Lamento y condeno enérgicamente los comentarios realizados en directo esta noche durante la retransmisión de las WTA Finals. Estos comentarios no reflejan los valores de beIN SPORTS. Reafirmo nuestro compromiso de tratar a todos los deportistas y colaboradores que participan en nuestras retransmisiones con respeto", compartió Houzot. Sabalenka, ganadora de cuatro títulos de Grand Slam que tiene 5,7 millones de seguidores en Instagram, no se ha pronunciado sobre la polémica. Este es el segundo incidente provocado por un micrófono abierto que sacude al tenis recientemente. El anterior involucró a Jessica Pegula, quien fue sorprendida mientras cotilleaba sobre Andreeva. La tenista estadounidense, heredera de una fortuna multimillonaria, fue captada por un micrófono durante un entrenamiento previo al torneo, calificando a Andreeva de "diva" que "necesita que le bajen los humos". Asimismo, confesó haber "perdido el respeto" por la legendaria jugadora española Conchita Martínez, actual entrenadora de Andreeva, quien este año se proclamó campeona de Roland Garros.

articles.title: Linda Noskova overtakes Alex Eala’s record after beating Coco Gauff at the WTA Finals
articles.summary: Linda Noskova has qualified for the semi-finals of the WTA Finals at the first time of asking. The Czech star, who won the Wimbledon title...
articles.body:
Linda Noskova has qualified for the semi-finals of the WTA Finals at the first time of asking.

The Czech star, who won the Wimbledon title earlier this year , defeated Coco Gauff 6-3, 6-3 on Tuesday evening.

Noskova , who also beat Marta Kostyuk earlier this week, now has a 2-0 record at the end-of-year event.

The 21-year-old will look to secure her spot as the group winner when she plays Jessica Pegula on Thursday.

Linda Noskova has won 25 matches since the start of the grass season

No player has been more successful on the WTA Tour since the start of the grass season than Czech superstar Linda Noskova.

Noskova has now won 25 matches across eight events, winning the Berlin Open and Wimbledon.

With victory against Coco Gauff on Tuesday, Noskova became the outright leader in this statistical category, moving one win ahead of Filipina prodigy Alexandra Eala .

Elena Rybakina, Jessica Pegula and Coco Gauff make up the top five.

Most match wins since the start of the grass-court swing

Noskova will look to add a 26th victory when she plays Jessica Pegula later this week. Noskova has a 3-1 record against Pegula, with her only defeat to the American occurring in the 2025 Bad Homburg Open semi-finals.

Pegula, who is currently second in the group, will look to secure her place in the semi-finals with victory against the Czech star.

Linda Noskova's last match vs Jessica Pegula

Noskova and Pegula last played each other at the 2026 Berlin Open.

Pegula defeated Katerina Siniakova, Madison Keys and Aryna Sabalenka en route to the final. Noskova beat Renata Zarazua, Diane Parry, Paula Badosa and Alexandra Eala.

Noskova emerged victorious from the final, beating Pegula 6-4, 4-6, 6-3.

"Jess, she's a very tricky player," Noskova said after the final. "She never gives up. She has a really good game for grass, so I obviously had to account for that fact, that it wasn't going to be easy at all.

"I will not give her the win, and she will not give me the win either. It was going to be one of those really tough matches that we always play.

"I'm very relieved I made it through this one."

Coco Gauff and Marta Kostyuk will be the first on court on Thursday. The American and Ukrainian are due to contest their final match at 12pm local time.

Jessica Pegula and Linda Noskova will contest their match following the conclusion of Gauff vs Kostyuk.

articles.title: ATP Finals in Turin: Format, players, schedule, prize money and draw as Carlos Alcaraz leads the field at end-of-season event
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev chases a third crown at the season-ending tournament, while Carlos Alcaraz targets his first with Ben Shelton, Daniil Medvedev and Frances Tiafoe also involved; The ATP Finals from Turin is live on Sky Sports Tennis from 15-22 November
articles.body:
World No 1 Alexander Zverev is chasing his third crown at the event, while Carlos Alcaraz will try to lift the trophy in Turin for the first time.

Ben Shelton, Daniil Medvedev, Flavio Cobolli, Arthur Fils, Frances Tiafoe and Rafael Jodar make up the field.

The tournament has been contested in major cities around the world, with a rich history dating back to the birth of The Masters in Tokyo (1970), and continues this year at Turin's Inalpi Arena.

The Nitto ATP Finals is structured as a round-robin format, with eight singles players/doubles teams divided into two groups of four.

All singles matches are the best of three tie-break sets. All doubles matches are best of three sets, with the first two sets played as tie-break sets with no ads and the final set played as a match tie-break.

The top seeded player/team is placed in Group A and the second seeded player/team is placed in Group B. The remaining players/teams are then drawn in pairs with the first drawn placed in Group A and the second drawn placed in Group B.

Each player/team plays the three other players/teams in his group.

The winner of each group is placed in separate semi-final brackets, with the top player/team in Group A playing the runner-up in Group B, and vice versa.

The draw will be made on Thursday, 12 November at 1pm

Players earn 200 points per round-robin match victory, 400 points for a semi-final win and 500 points for winning the tournament

Main Draw Round-Robin Matches: Sunday November 15 - Friday November 20

Afternoon session starts at 12.30am (doubles), 3pm (singles)

Evening session 7pm (doubles), not before 9.30pm (singles)

Afternoon session starts at 1pm (doubles), 3.30pm (singles). Evening session not before 7pm (doubles), not before 9.30pm (singles)

Doubles final at 4pm and singles final at 7pm

Undefeated Champion: £3,850,000 Final Win: £1,800,000 Semi-Final Win: £900,000,000 Each Round-Robin Match Win: £300,000 Participation Fee: £250,000* Alternate:£115,000 [*Pro-rated on a per-match basis: 1 match: £125,000 | 2 matches: £190,000 | 3 matches: £250,000]

Most titles, singles: Novak Djokovic (7)

Oldest champion: Novak Djokovic, 36, in 2023

Youngest champion: John McEnroe, 19, in 1978

Highest-ranked champion: No. 1s Ilie Nastase (1973), Jimmy Connors (1977), Bjorn Borg (1979-80), John McEnroe (1984), Ivan Lendl (1985-87), Pete Sampras (1994, 1996-97), Lleyton Hewitt (2002), Roger Federer (2004, 2006-07), Novak Djokovic (2012, 2014-15), Andy Murray (2016) and Jannik Sinner (2024)

Lowest-ranked champion: No. 12 David Nalbandian in 2005

Last home champion: Jannik Sinner in Turin in 2025

Brits Henry Patten and Neal Skupski have both qualified.

articles.summary: Se disputará junto a Rafa Jódar la condición de número dos del equipo español en Bolonia
articles.body: Alejandro Davidovich, 17 del ranking a sus 27 años y flamante campeón esta temporada del Mallorca Championship, Chengdu y el Masters 1000 de Shanghái, regresó el martes a los entrenamientos, según ha podido saber MARCA, con la vista puesta en la fase final de la Copa Davis (24 al 29). El tenista del Rincón de la Victoria es uno de los cinco convocados por parte del capitán David Ferrer para intentar reconquistar la máxima competición por países, que España no gana desde 2019. Davidovich, que tuvo que poner punto y final a la temporada 2026 en el circuito antes de tiempo por un virus estomacal que no le permitió jugar en Basilea, y unos posteriores dolores en la espalda que le bajaron de París, tiene una gran ilusión en levantar la prestigiosa Ensaladera de plata. Ferrer ya ha avisado que Álex y Rafa Jódar se jugarán en Bolonia la condición de número dos de la Armada. La de líder está reservada a Carlos Alcaraz. La selección nacional tiene previsto concentrarse en la sede de las finales el próximo sábado 21 y un día más tarde iniciará las sesiones preparatorias. España debuta en los cuartos el 26 contra Austria.

articles.title: WTA Finals: Aryna Sabalenka stunned by Mirra Andreeva as Elina Svitolina battles back vs Karolina Muchova at Indian Wells
articles.summary: Wednesday sees Aryna Sabalenka suffer stunning collapse in WTA Finals thrashing by Mirra Andreeva; Elina Svitolina staged comeback vs Karolina Muchova; Cam Norrie beaten by Taylor Fritz at Stockholm Open; Watch WTA Finals from Indian Wells this week on Sky Sports Tennis
articles.body:
Andreeva, the 19-year-old French Open champion, won her second straight ​Group 2 match and advanced as group ‌winner after Svitolina earlier defeated Muchova 3-6 6-2 6-2.

The result eliminated Muchova from ​semi-final contention, while Svitolina will face Sabalenka in Friday's final group match with the remaining place in the last ​four at stake.

Sabalenka, the world No 2 ⁠and US Open runner-up, made ⁠the stronger start and broke Andreeva in the fourth game of a closely fought ‌opening set to move 3-1 ahead.

Andreeva responded immediately, however, winning three consecutive games to draw level at 4-4 before breaking ‌Sabalenka again and serving out the set.

The Russian maintained the momentum in the second set, capitalising on Sabalenka's errors to break early and race into a 3-0 lead.

Andreeva did not ⁠allow Sabalenka another game, sealing a dominant ​victory on her WTA Finals debut.

Svitolina battles back to beat Muchova and keep WTA Finals title hopes alive

Svitolina staged a remarkable comeback to beat Muchova and remain in the hunt for the WTA Finals title.

The Ukrainian looked to be on her way out of Indian Wells when she was a set down and required an eight-minute medical time-out. But she recovered to win 3-6 6-2 6-2 and stay in with a chance of reaching the semi-finals.

Svitolina, who was demolished 6-4 6-0 by Mirra Andreeva in her opening round-robin match, told Sky Sports : "It was not an easy task to do.

"I was pretty angry at myself, to be fair, after the first match and after the first set also. Things didn't go my way, so I tried to direct this anger towards the ball and found my game in the end.

"I played good. I think the level was back in the third set. I just tried to give it all in this match because I know I would be eliminated if I lost.

"So I just tried to really release all this energy and find, you know, these openings against Karolina. She's such a tough opponent.

"It's the last tournament of the season, so you know, I just have to really put my head down and deal with all the small injuries.

"I mean, it's normal that everyone is tired. Everyone is struggling with something here and there. I will just try to do my best, have an ice bath and try to heal as much as possible in like 48 hours."

Britain's Norrie beaten by Fritz at Stockholm Open

Britain's Cameron Norrie was knocked out of the Stockholm Open on Wednesday following a straight-sets defeat to Taylor Fritz in the round of 16.

World No 10 Fritz battled to clinch the first set 7-5 and subsequently wrapped up the win with a 6-3 victory in the second set to book his spot in the quarter-finals.

Norrie reached Tuesday's last-16 clash with a straight-sets win over James Duckworth in the opening round, while No 1 seed Fritz received a bye into the second round.

Fritz started the match strongly with two aces to hold in the opening game, but had his serve broken by Norrie in the third game.

The Briton strengthened his grip as he held his serve, but Fritz replied with a break of his own to take the contest to 5-5.

He piled on the pressure, serving three aces in the following game and broke Norrie's serve in the 12th game to win the first set.

A tight tussle saw little separate the pair in the second set until Norrie had his serve broken in the eighth game and Fritz subsequently held serve to see out the match.

articles.title: Emma Raducanu to return at United Cup in January after lengthy injury absence
articles.summary: Emma Raducanu will make her return to tennis in the United Cup team competition in Australia in the first week of 2027.
articles.body:
Emma Raducanu will make her return to tennis in the United Cup team competition in Australia in the first week of 2027.

Britain's 2021 US Open champion has not played since June because of a stress fracture of the shin.

Raducanu was beaten by Croatia’s Donna Vekic in her first grass-court final at Queen's Club on 14 June, but had to pull out of Wimbledon on the eve of her opening match just 14 days later.

The 23-year-old contemplated playing a couple of events in Asia this autumn but, by delaying her return until January, she will be able to use a special ranking of 38 to enter tournaments.

A special ranking is available to players who have been out with injury for at least six months. In Raducanu's case, it reflects her position in the world rankings after Wimbledon, as she received some prize money despite not playing a match there.

The current British number five will be able to use a special ranking to enter eight events next year, including two Grand Slams and five WTA 1000 tournaments.

Her actual ranking of 107 would likely be too low to make the main draw of January's Australian Open and most other WTA Tour events.

But with a special ranking, Raducanu will not only be assured of playing in Melbourne but also at the WTA 1000 events in Doha, Dubai, Indian Wells and Miami which follow in February and March.

The entry deadline for the United Cup passed on Monday, shortly after Raducanu had her application for a special ranking approved.

A ranking of 38 will make her the British number one for the purposes of this event, giving her the chance to play alongside Arthur Fery in a competition featuring 18 national teams.

Francesca Jones, Jan Choinski and doubles players Neal Skupski and Olivia Nicholls complete the British team for the tournament, which takes place from 1-10 January.

Britain will play Australia and France in their group matches in Sydney, and Raducanu can expect to be face current top-40 players Talia Gibson and Diane Parry.

'I don't fear for my safety from online abuse - because we're so used to it'

Raducanu made a gradual return to training in early September - and four months is a long time to train without any competitive action.

She may also not play any exhibitions between now and the end of the year but a spell of warm weather training is anticipated, with the Middle East a popular destination for players in the run-up to the Australian Open.

Recent practice sessions in London with head coach Andrew Richardson and LTA national coach Alex Ward have been increasing in intensity, according to observers.

But by the time Raducanu returns, she will have been on the sidelines for over six months. Playing a few tournaments in Asia would have helped her regain some match sharpness, and perhaps allowed for a faster start to 2027.

Her fellow Briton Sonay Kartal is a fine example, having enjoyed considerable success since returning from six months out with a stress fracture of the back in September.

After reaching the third round of the China Open in her first WTA Tour event back, she beat world number six Elina Svitolina and then world number 12 Belinda Bencic on her way to the Wuhan Open final.

Kartal says there were a "lot of conversations" about where she should make a return.

"I think I wanted to just go straight in. I trusted that I would be able to get my level back, I just didn't know how quickly," the 25-year-old said.

"But I still think there is a long way to go. I can produce the level, but can I sustain it?

"Rehab is draining, and the body is not used to a lot of matches on the tour, so I do feel the aches and the pains from that."

There will only be 24 candles on Raducanu’s birthday cake later this week, but there is no escaping the amount of time she has missed since her stunning New York victory as a teenage qualifier.

She has averaged just 31 matches a season in the five years since that triumph. Players with aspirations to be inside the world's top 20 would hope to play around twice that number.

Elena Rybakina, for example, played 68 matches across 20 tournaments this year as she rose to the top of the world rankings for the first time.

By contrast, Raducanu played just 21 matches, losing in the second round of the Australian Open and the first round at Roland Garros.

Last year, Raducanu contested a career-best 50 matches, and earlier this year rose to 23 in the rankings shortly after reaching the final in the Romanian city of Cluj.

But her early preparation was affected by bone bruising of the foot, and she did not play for two months between March and May because of a post-viral illness picked up in Cluj.

Raducanu said a stress fracture of the shin was only confirmed after a final scan on the night before Wimbledon. But in her desperation to play, she had continued to train at times in the run-up to the championships, when medical advice had suggested that might be unwise.

articles.body: La United Cup 2027 ya tiene fechas y equipos. Se celebrará del 1 al 10 de enero, en Perth y Sidney, y tendrá un total de 18 selecciones en liza. España será una de ellas y MARCA puede adelantar que el equipo español estará liderado por Rafa Jódar. Todo eso le ha valido la atención de marcas tan prestigiosas como Rolex, que le han fichado como uno de sus embajadores. España ha ido a parar al grupo F, junto a Bélgica y Argentina. Otros nombres destacados que estarán en el certamen mixto son Ben Shelton, Flavio Cobolli y Felix Auger-Aliassime o Emma Raducanu, entre otros. articles.title: WTA Finals: Mirra Andreeva thrashes Aryna Sabalenka, Elina Svitolina beats Karolina Muchova
articles.summary: Mirra Andreeva wins 11 games in a row to thrash world number two Aryna Sabalenka and reach the last four at the WTA Finals.
articles.body:
Mirra Andreeva won 11 games in a row as she thrashed world number two Aryna Sabalenka to reach the last four at the WTA Finals.

French Open champion Andreeva was 4-1 down in the opening set before producing some superb tennis and taking advantage of an increasingly erratic Sabalenka performance.

The 19-year-old Russian went on to deliver a statement 6-4 6-0 victory over four-time major singles winner Sabalenka.

"I will be honest, I feel like Aryna did not have the best day," Andreeva told Sky Sports.

"I feel like I cannot really take all the credit today - I feel like that is not very fair in some ways.

"I'm just happy. I had a goal in front of me to commit no matter what and control the things I can control."

As poor as Sabalenka was, Andreeva produced a mature, intelligent performance to shut her out of the match.

She used loopy high balls to initially wrong-foot Sabalenka and then showcased her easy power, hitting 16 winners to only six unforced errors and creating brilliant angles from the baseline.

The only blip came when she found herself 15-30 down as she served for the first set. However, Andreeva calmly hit three aces in a row to take the lead and never looked back.

Second seed Sabalenka had taping on her knee but it did not seem to hinder her - this, rather, was a performance similar to some of the collapses she has had this year.

From having a double-break lead, Sabalenka only won a further 10 points in the match as Andreeva dominated.

The Belarusian hit 23 unforced errors and failed to produce a single ace at Indian Wells, where she won the WTA Tour title earlier this year.

Sabalenka lost deciding sets at the French Open and Berlin Open by a 6-0 scoreline this year, but this was a much quicker unravelling than those matches.

The result means the winner of the final group match on Friday between Sabalenka and Elina Svitolina will advance to the semi-finals, while Andreeva goes through as the group winner.

Svitolina channels 'anger' to inspire comeback win

Svitolina said she "got a bit angry at myself" to inspire a comeback victory over Karolina Muchova and keep her title hopes alive.

Ukraine's Svitolina lost 6-4 6-0 in her first group match against Andreeva on Monday and made an equally poor start against Muchova.

It looked as though things were getting worse for Svitolina when she took a medical timeout for a right hip injury after losing the first set, before finding herself an early break point down.

However, the sixth seed saved it and then gradually wore down Wimbledon runner-up Muchova to win 3-6 6-2 6-2.

Muchova hit 39 unforced errors throughout the match - the majority of which came from her forehand - as Svitolina ground her down.

Svitolina made no mistake, with the 32-year-old tipping her head back and roaring in celebration after securing the win.

"I was really angry at myself after the first match and the first set," Svitolina told Sky Sports.

"Sometimes it [channelling frustration] happens in a good way and sometimes in a bad way.

"I tried to direct my anger towards the ball and I found my game in the end."

At the Stockholm Open, Britain's Cameron Norrie fell 7-5 6-3 to world number 10 Taylor Fritz.

Denmark's Holger Rune reached the quarter-finals of the tournament, a year after he ruptured his Achilles at the same event.

Rune only made his return to the ATP Tour in October after a gruelling 12 months recovering from the injury, but beat Miomir Kecmanovic 2-6 6-1 6-4 to advance.

articles.title: Andreeva powers past Sabalenka to reach WTA Finals last four
articles.summary: French Open champion Mirra Andreeva stormed past Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 6-0 to reach the last four of the WTA Finals on Wednesday as Elina Svitolina kept her b...
articles.body:
French Open champion Mirra Andreeva stormed past Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 6-0 to reach the last four of the WTA Finals on Wednesday as Elina Svitolina kept her bid on track with a three-set win over Karolina Muchova.

Russian 19-year-old Andreeva held her nerve after falling behind 4-1 in the opening set -- winning the last 11 games to seal the round-robin victory in just 62 minutes.

"Oh my God, I'm even happier than I was after my first match," Andreeva said. "I feel like I can play another two matches, I'm so full of energy. I'm so pumped up. I'm so happy."

Andreeva, whose three titles this year include her maiden major at Roland Garros, is making her singles debut in the elite season-ending event.

The world number three seemed to be feeling the nerves in the early going against second-ranked Sabalenka.

Irked that she had given up a break with a double fault, she was able to flip the switch, dealing handily with Sabalenka's big serves and pushing the Belarusian star back with her own big groundstrokes.

Andreeva crucially kept momentum on her side with a break for a 3-0 lead in the second set.

Sabalenka, trailing 0-40, saved three break points, but Andreeva gave herself another with a swinging volley winner and grabbed another break when a Sabalenka forehand flew just long.

The increasingly demoralized Sabalenka had no answer. After the Belarusian smacked a backhand into the net to give her opponent match point Andreeva polished things off with a service winner.

It was another disappointing performance for the 28-year-old Sabalenka, whose three wins this season include prestigious back-to-back victories at Indian Wells and Miami but no Grand Slams.

Making her sixth straight Finals appearance, Sabalenka can still advance if she beats Svitolina in their final round-robin match on Friday.

Svitolina roared back from a set down to beat Muchova 3-6, 6-2, 6-2.

Ukrainian veteran Svitolina lifted the WTA Finals trophy in 2018 but hadn't been back to the elite season-ending event since 2019.

She got off to a rocky start against Muchova, who broke Svitolina three times in the opening set.

Trailing 2-1 on serve in the second Svitolina found her range, winning five straight games to force a third set.

"I was not happy with the first set," Svitolina said. "I didn't play as well. I just made some adjustments, tactical adjustments.

"I think it helped me also to be more aggressive, because I was too passive in the first set," Svitolina said.

Muchova's second round-robin defeat coupled with Andreeva's victory means the Czech was eliminated from semi-final contention.

articles.title: Aryna Sabalenka must end a troubling trend in her matches
articles.summary: It happened again at the 2026 WTA Finals
articles.body:
WTA World No. 2 Aryna Sabalenka was unstoppable this spring winning the Sunshine Double. Many thought the reigning Indian Wells champion would be the odds-on favorite to win her first WTA Finals title because she plays some of her best tennis on the Indian Wells hardcourts.

Mirra Andreeva, the 2025 Indian Wells champion, played the best match of her season against Sabalenka in the second round of the 2026 WTA Finals round robin action. Down 1-4, Andreeva won 11 straight games to win the match 6-4, 6-0.

A startling statistic from that match has plagued Sabalenka too often this year.

It is shocking that a player with Sabalenka's talent, power, and serve got bageled for the third time in 2026.

Sabalenka was bageled in back-to-back losses in June at Roland Garros against Diana Shnaider and at Berlin against Jessica Pegula.

Players are handling her power game which frustrates her

Sabalenka added some finesse shots to her game. She is trying to keep her opponents off balance and unsure what is coming at them.

However, players are adjusting to her power game which frustrates her. Sabalenka spent the last couple of years earning lopsided wins. She is not accustomed to being on the losing end in a similar fashion.

Sabalenka is a great champion, and we cannot wait to see how she evolves her game to overcome this in 2027.

articles.title: El duelo de las víctimas de los audios filtrados: Sabalenka pierde 11 juegos seguidos y sucumbe ante Andreeva
articles.standfirst: Andreeva, que debuta en unas Finales de la WTA en individuales, se asegura un puesto en semifinales como ganadora del Grupo 2
articles.summary: Andreeva, que debuta en unas Finales de la WTA en individuales, se asegura un puesto en semifinales como ganadora del Grupo 2
articles.body: La rusa Mirra Andreeva y la bielorrusa Aryna Sabalenka, las protagonistas involuntarias de los dos audios filtrados que han sacudido al mundo del tenis, se han enfrentado en las Masters WTA Finals. La rusa Mirra Andreeva desarboló a Aryna Sabalenka con 11 juegos consecutivos y se clasificó para las semifinales de las Finales de la WTA, que se disputan en Indian Wells (Estados Unidos), como ganadora del Grupo 2. Andreeva, número 3 del mundo, derrotó a Sabalenka por 6-4 y 6-0 en apenas 62 minutos de partido. Sabalenka tenía el primer set encarrilado con un 4-1 arriba con un 'break' de ventaja, cuando Andreeva reaccionó de forma arrolladora y encadenó once juegos consecutivos para imponerse por 6-4 y 6-0. La rusa ganó 45 de los 55 puntos disputados desde el 4-1. Andreeva terminó con 16 ganadores y solo 6 errores no forzados, por solo 8 ganadores y 23 errores no forzados de Sabalenka. "Estoy incluso más contenta que tras mi primer partido. Siento que podría jugar otros dos partidos. Estoy llena de energía, muy motivada y muy feliz", aseguró la rusa en declaraciones a pie de pista. Con este triunfo, Andreeva, que debuta en unas Finales de la WTA en individuales, se asegura un puesto en semifinales como ganadora del Grupo 2 y espera rival del Grupo 1 entre la checa Linda Noskova (n.8) -que ya está clasificada- o las estadounidenses Coco Gauff (n.4) y Jessica Pegula (n.5). Por su lado, Sabalenka se disputará la segunda plaza del Grupo 2 este viernes en la última jornada contra la ucraniana Elina Svitolina (n.6). Ambas suman una victoria y una derrota en las dos primeras jornadas. Svitolina también tuvo que remontar este miércoles, en su caso a la checa Karolina Muchova (n.7), por 3-6, 6-2 y 6-2 en 2 horas y 2 minutos. Con la derrota, Muchova queda fuera de la pugna por las semifinales. Andreeva y Noskova, las dos por ahora semifinalistas, son vigentes campeonas de Roland Garros y Wimbledon. La ganadora de los otros dos 'grandes' del año (Australia y Estados Unidos), la kazaja Elena Rybakina, es baja en el torneo por enfermedad. Además de ganadora en Melbourne y Nueva York, Rybakina es la número uno del mundo y vigente campeona de las Finales WTA.

articles.title: Marcel Granollers: "La palabra retirada estuvo en mi cabeza este año"
articles.standfirst: El barcelonés se ha clasificado para las ATP Finals al lado de Zeballos por séptima vez seguida
articles.summary: El barcelonés se ha clasificado para las ATP Finals al lado de Zeballos por séptima vez seguida
articles.body: Marcel Granollers, a sus 40 años, se ha clasificado por séptima vez seguida para las ATP Finals al lado de Horacio Zeballos. El barcelonés, triple campeón de Grand Slam, se sienta con MARCA para hablar de la cita de maestros de Turín y la fase final de la Copa Davis. Pregunta. ¿La regularidad que están teniendo en cuanto a presencias en este torneo espera que sea recompensada con el título? Respuesta. Ojalá. Siempre se va con la esperanza de obtener un buen resultado. Clasificarnos es un objetivo que tienes a principios de año. Una vez empecemos, vamos a intentar dar el máximo para obtener un buen resultado. P. ¿El vencedor está más abierto que nunca al haber las ocho mejores parejas del curso? R. El dobles es una modalidad que está bastante abierta. Somos un grupo de parejas que optamos a ganar títulos. El tipo de superficie, el formato y la igualdad da para que pueda ganar cualquiera de los que estamos aquí. P. De Carlos Alcaraz se dice que es favorito porque llega más fresco que los demás al haber estado lesionado. Usted y Zeballos sólo han jugado París desde el US Open. ¿Puede haber un paralelismo? R. El haber jugado poco nos da esa frescura, esas ganas por querer jugar bien a final de año. Después esto no garantiza nada porque el deporte, el tenis y el dobles es muy igualado. Llegamos con ganas de jugar y sin semanas seguidas compitiendo. Espero que esto juegue a nuestro favor. P. A sus edad y habiendo sido maestro en 2012, ¿tiene las mismas ganas por volver a coronarse? R. La motivación es la misma porque con Horacio es la séptima participación, llegamos una vez a la final, tenemos dos semifinales... Hemos estado cerquita y es una ilusión conseguirlo con él. Hemos ganado torneos de todas las categorías y este nos falta y ojalá lo podamos ganar este año. P. Ustedes han ganado dos veces en Roland Garros y una en el US Open. ¿Es realista pensar en completar el Grand Slam? R. Nos costó muchísimo ganar el primer grande y sería bonito ganar en Australia y en Wimbledon en 2027. Con la edad que tenemos es importante tener estas motivaciones, pero que no sean una presión. No puedes ir a Australia y meterte una presión extrema que no te deje jugar. Pero en el día a día hay que querer evolucionar. P. Cada campaña que pasa está más cerca de colgar la raqueta. ¿La palabra retirada ha estado presente en su cabeza este curso? R. Al final vas cumpliendo años y te preguntas cosas o piensas en cómo va a ser tu futuro. Hay momentos de todo. Sí que es verdad que este año la palabra retirada la he tenido en la cabeza y he reflexionado sobre ello. Pero hay motivaciones que me gustaría cumplir y es lo que me ha hecho decidir seguir compitiendo el año que viene e intentar conseguir las cosas que me faltan. P. ¿La palabra retirada del equipo de la Copa Davis se la ha planteado? R. Si sigo jugando es por cosas como la Copa Davis, que me llena, me motiva. Son de los objetivos que uno tiene ilusión por conseguir. Son semanas especiales porque no solemos jugar en equipo, por tu país, lo hacemos en semanas puntuales y sientes esa energía que te hace sentir vivo. Después ya depende del capitán que te seleccione o no. P. Usted es fijo en el dobles de España. ¿La mejor pareja es Marcel con Alcaraz? R. Es una pregunta más para el capitán que para mí. Por suerte, en el equipo tenemos grandes jugadores y David puede hace varias parejas que rendirían al máximo nivel si tienen que jugar. Los jugadores convocados tenemos cualidades suficientes para adaptarnos a varias parejas que formemos entre nosotros. P. ¿Acepta el cartel de favoritos en Bolonia? R. Yo creo que vamos con un muy buen equipo, con ganas de hacerlo bien. Lo sé porque hemos hablado entre nosotros. Tenemos un grandísimo equipo, pero sabemos cómo es el deporte. Cada día tenemos que ofrecer un gran nivel porque las selecciones que hay son muy potentes. Están algunos de los mejores jugadores del mundo y son partidos igualados que se deciden por detalles. P. Usted es el único de la convocatoria de la selección que ya sabe lo que es levantar la Ensaladera. ¿Les va a explicar a sus compañeros lo que eso significa? R. Hay jugadores que han conseguido cosas que yo no he conseguido y tienen toda la experiencia del mundo en situaciones difíciles y de máxima tensión. A tenistas de su nivel y de su ranking no creo que les tenga que explicar mucho porque ya han tenido resultados enormes.

Precisamente será este último el acompañante del madrileño este jueves en su primer entrenamiento en la sede de la cita de maestros. Tienen reservada pista durante una hora en la central. Tiafoe y Jódar, que fueron los dos últimos en clasificarse para el 'round robin', no se pueden cruzar en la fase de grupos, cuyo sorteo se realizará hoy en la capital de la región del Piamonte. Rafa, revelación de la presente temporada al conseguir ser el primer jugador que acaba entre los ocho mejores en su debut como profesional, tiene un 50 por ciento de posibilidades de debutar con su compatriota Carlos Alcaraz. Y es que una de las reglas de competición es que los cabezas de serie 1 y 2 se enfrenten en su primer partido al 7 y 8, que en este caso son Tiafoe y Jódar. articles.summary: Carlitos completa su grupo con Medvedev y Cobolli mientras que Rafa se las verá con Sascha, Shelton y Fils
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz y Rafa Jódar han conocido este jueves su grupo en las ATP Finals de Turín 2026 donde no podrán verse las caras hasta unas hipotéticas semifinales. Alcaraz ha ido a parar al grupo Ivan Lendl, con Daniil Medvedev, Flavio Cobolli y Frances Tiafoe. Estos dos últimos debutan en el torneo. El murciano, en su cuarta presencia seguida en la cita de maestros, se estrenará el lunes con Frances Tiafoe, el número ocho del ranking a sus 28 años y uno de los cuatro debutantes en el torneo. Alcaraz y Tiafoe se han enfrentado entre ocasiones y el primero domina el cara a cara por dos victorias a una. Para encontrar el único triunfo del estadounidense hay que remontarse al Godó de 2021, cuando el fenómeno de El Palmar sólo tenía 17 años. El buen rollo entre ambos ha hecho que se hayan medido también en tres exhibiciones y todas cayeron del lado de Frances: dos en Estados Unidos (Charlotte 2024 y Nueva Jersey 2025) y en Hurlingham, en 2022. Cobolli se las verá de inicio con Medvedev. El pupilo de Samuel López le tiene ganado el cara a cara a todos los rivales de Turín a excepción de Jódar con el que nunca se enfrentó: Tiafoe (2-1), Cobolli (1-0), Medvedev (7-3), Zverev (7-6), Shelton (4-1) y Fils (3-0). Rafa Jódar ha ido a parar al grupo John McEnroe y tendrá su primer partido en la jornada inaugural del domingo, a las 14:00 horas, con el número 1, Alexander Zverev. Un único precedente entre ambos, que cayó del lado del alemán en los cuartos del último Roland Garros. El cartel lo completan Ben Shelton y Arthur Fils. Marcel Granollers y Horacio Zeballos, terceros cabezas de serie y que encadenan siete participaciones, han ido a parar al grupo Woodforde, junto a Christian Harrison y Neil Skupski, Simone Bolelli y Andrea Vavassori y Kevin Krawietz y Tim Puet. Estos últimos son los vigentes campeones. El primer partido de la pareja hispano-argentina será frente a los locales Vavassori y Bolelli, que han decidido separar sus caminos a la conclusión de la presente temporada.

articles.title: Lucy Shuker: British wheelchair tennis player retires after 24-year career
articles.summary: British wheelchair tennis player Lucy Shuker retires after 24 years as a professional and three Paralympic medals.
articles.body:
British wheelchair tennis player Lucy Shuker has retired after 24 years as a professional and three Paralympic medals.

The 46-year-old represented GB at five consecutive Paralympics and won one silver medal and two bronze between 2012 and 2020, in the women's doubles alongside Jordanne Whiley.

A nine-time Grand Slam finalist and seven-time World Team Cup medalist, Shuker announced during Wimbledon this year that she would retire at the end of the season.

At the time she had 98 doubles titles and achieved her aim of reaching 100 earlier this month, when she and Ruby Bishop won at the WC50 Abingdon in Oxfordshire. Shuker also won 39 singles titles.

She was awarded the British Empire Medal for services to sport in 2023 and was GB's flagbearer for the opening ceremony of the 2024 Paralympics in Paris.

"I would like to congratulate Lucy on her fantastic career and thank her for the contribution she has made to wheelchair tennis both on and off the court," said the LTA's chief executive Scott Lloyd.

"To compete at the highest level of the game for over 20 years is a remarkable achievement and testament to her dedication and professionalism.

"She has been, and will continue to be, a passionate advocate for the development of the sport and we look forward to working with her to continue to grow the game for future generations."

Her last match came on Wednesday at the Wheelchair Tennis Finals in Barcelona, where she and Ksenia Chasteau were beaten 6-3 6-1 by the Dutch pair of Diede de Groot and Aniek Van Koot.

Shuker lived and trained in Somerset for much of her career, spending most of it ranked just outside the world's top 10. She retires ranked 23rd in the world, the British number two behind Cornelia Oosthuizen (20).

El madrileño, en su estreno en la competición reservada a los ocho mejores del curso, jugará su primer partido ante Alexander Zverev, número 1 mundial, en la jornada inaugural del domingo 15. Jódar y Zverev se han enfrentado en una única ocasión en el circuito, con triunfo de Sascha en los cuartos de la última edición de Roland Garros. Zverev es uno de los dos tenistas presentes en Turín que ya sabe lo que es inscribir su nombre en el palmarés. Lo hizo en las ediciones de 2018 y 2021. El tenista natural de Hamburgo, de 29 años, termina la temporada como líder del ranking ATP por delante de Jannik Sinner y Carlos Alcaraz. articles.title: What Maria Sharapova’s luxury lifestyle reveals about her success: From $38.8 million in tennis prize money and Sugarpova to business investments, luxury real estate and family support
articles.summary: Explore how Maria Sharapova transitioned from a five-time Grand Slam winner to a successful entrepreneur, with a fortune of $220 million derived from endorsements, business ventures, and strategic investments in luxury real estate.
articles.body: Maria Sharapova’s dollars have little to do with her tennis accomplishments. She retired in 2020 after five Grand Slams and a global profile that brought major sponsorships and led her into business and investment interests. Her career earnings from prize money, endorsements and appearances were estimated at $325 million.Her lifestyle is one of the conversion from elite athlete to entrepreneur and investor. Sharapova has used her sporting fame to build a second career in high-value property, a connection to luxury fashion and her own confectionery brand, Sugarpova, giving a glimpse of her off-court empire.What Maria Sharapova’s $220 million fortune reveals about her luxury lifestyleAccording to Celebrity Net Worth, Maria Sharapova has an estimated net worth of approximately $220 million. Her wealth reflects several income streams developed during and after her professional tennis career.In 2004 Sharapova was a rising international star after beating Serena Williams to win Wimbledon at just 17 years of age. She would win five Grand Slam singles titles, 36 WTA singles titles and the world No. 1 ranking. Her achievements attracted major endorsement partnerships, including Nike, Porsche, Evian, and TAG Heuer.Forbes estimated her total career earnings at approximately $325 million by the time she retired in 2020. That figure included commercial income as well as tennis prize money. Her career prize money alone was approximately $38.8 million, making endorsements and other commercial opportunities particularly important to her financial story.What Maria Sharapova owns beyond her tennis careerSharapova’s real estate choices reflect an interest in architecture and design alongside luxury living. One of her best-known property projects was a custom-built, Japanese-inspired mansion in Manhattan Beach, California.She purchased the ocean-view lot in 2012 for approximately $4.1 million and worked closely on the design of the three-story property. The home included distinctive features such as a bowling alley. It was later sold in 2025 to basketball star Luka Dončić for a reported $25 million, according to the supplied property reports.Her passion for design has also been translated into the fashion and luxury business. In 2025, reports highlighted her appointment to the board of Moncler Group, adding a corporate leadership dimension to her connection with the luxury industry.How Maria Sharapova turned business interests into investmentsSugarpova became one of Sharapova’s most recognizable ventures. Launched in 2012, the confectionery brand turned her personal interest in candy into a commercial business. Forbes reported that she invested her own money in the venture and remained closely involved in its development.Her investment interests have also included companies in wellness, fitness, and consumer products. Reports have linked her to businesses such as Supergoop!, Therabody, and Tonal. These investments illustrate an approach that extends beyond traditional athlete endorsements, although the value of individual stakes has not been publicly established.How family support shaped Maria Sharapova’s successSharapova’s financial discipline is often traced to the early sacrifices of her family. Her father, Yuri Sharapov, came to the United States with her from Russia when she was just seven years old and had limited resources to help her develop in tennis. Later, her mother Yelena joined them.That experience helped shape the work ethic that has driven her sporting career and her business decisions. Sharapova had commercial interests that would outlive her retirement, not just her tennis earnings. Her lavish lifestyle is therefore not only a result of sporting success, but also of a long-term effort to translate fame, business ownership and investment opportunities into lasting financial independence.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: WTA Finals: Coco Gauff battles through back injury to beat Marta Kostyuk
articles.summary: Coco Gauff shows all of her battling qualities as she fights through a back injury to beat Marta Kostyuk and keep her WTA Finals last-four hopes alive.
articles.body:
Coco Gauff showed all of her battling qualities as she fought through a back injury to beat Marta Kostyuk and keep her WTA Finals last-four hopes alive.

American Gauff was visibly in pain as she received treatment on her lower back midway through a match she needed to win to stay in the tournament.

She found herself 5-1 down in the second set - only to win six games in a row to complete a 6-4 7-5 win at Indian Wells.

"Physically, I wasn't at my best, which I'm not really used to," Gauff told Sky Sports.

"It was like a mental challenge, learning how to play through that."

The long tennis season has taken a toll on a number of players, with Ukraine's Kostyuk also receiving treatment on a wrist injury that has been hampering her since August.

It is the second time that Gauff has overturned a 5-1 deficit at this tournament, having done the same to beat Jessica Pegula on Sunday.

However, the 22-year-old admitted she was not expecting it to happen again, and was already preparing herself for a third set.

"I asked my physio at 5-2 down, what can I do on the bathroom break [between sets] to try and loosen up," Gauff said.

Gauff will need Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova to beat Pegula in the final group match if she is to reach the semi-finals.

Gauff struggled with her serve throughout, producing nine double faults to one ace, but said afterwards she struggled to get through her motion without feeling pain.

Kostyuk - a late call-up to the season-ending finals after Elena Rybakina's withdrawal - also struggled to generate pace and spin because of her wrist problem.

World number four Gauff came back from an early break down to take the first set, but immediately ran into problems in the second.

She called for the trainer after going 3-0 down but soon trailed by a double break, with Kostyuk saving three break points inbetween.

However, with her movement hampered and the crowd behind her, Gauff was able to swing hard and ultimately outlast Kostyuk.

articles.title: Coco Gauff makes ‘lucky’ admission on crazy 2nd-set comeback to beat Marta Kostyuk
articles.summary: Coco Gauff admitted she was already preparing for a third set before mounting a comeback against Marta Kostyuk on Thursday, winning six consecutive games to...
articles.body:
Coco Gauff admitted she was already preparing for a third set before mounting a comeback against Marta Kostyuk on Thursday, winning six consecutive games to secure a 6-4, 7-5 win in round-robin play at the WTA Finals .

Gauff trailed 5-1 in the second set before rallying to defeat Kostyuk in straight sets, overcoming serving struggles and requiring attention from a trainer during the match.

Afterward, Gauff acknowledged that she had nearly accepted the prospect of playing a deciding set before the momentum shifted in her favor.
