"I'm not going to lie, (my) head was already in that third set," Gauff said of her mindset when trailing 5-1, as reported by The Guardian. "Then once it got to 5-4 I was like, 'OK, I can win this set.' I got a little bit lucky. She gave me a few errors. I'm glad I was able to close that out."

Despite the win, Gauff's chances of advancing to the semifinals remained dependent on the outcome of Jessica Pegula's match against Linda Noskova later Thursday.

A win by Pegula, Gauff's former doubles partner, would eliminate Gauff and send Pegula into the semifinals. Gauff had previously defeated Pegula in three sets during their opening Group 1 match.

Noskova, the reigning Wimbledon champion, had already secured a semifinal berth at the season-ending tournament, which was relocated from Saudi Arabia to Southern California because of the war involving Iran in the Middle East.

Against Kostyuk, Gauff initially appeared headed for a more comfortable win after taking a 5-2 lead in the opening set. Kostyuk broke Gauff's serve to narrow the deficit to 5-4, but Gauff immediately broke back to claim the set.

Kostyuk responded by winning the first four games of the second set. Gauff struggled with double faults and received treatment from a trainer early in the set.

After falling behind 5-1, Gauff fought off three break points to hold serve and begin her comeback. She subsequently broke Kostyuk twice to level the score at 5-5 before holding for a 6-5 advantage.

Kostyuk entered the tournament as the first alternate following top-ranked Elena Rybakina's withdrawal because of a viral illness. The 24-year-old Ukrainian finished Group 1 play with an 0-3 record.

Reporting by Beth Harris of The Associated Press was referenced in this article.

articles.title: She is the only player who has lost 6-0 6-0 in the history of the WTA Finals
articles.summary: The WTA Finals have not always had close-fought matches throughout its history. Every year, the WTA season concludes with the WTA Finals, featuring the top.....
articles.body:
The WTA Finals have not always had close-fought matches throughout its history.

Every year, the WTA season concludes with the WTA Finals , featuring the top eight singles players and doubles teams to go head-to-head for one final tournament of the year.

The 2026 WTA Finals are already underway, and have seen world number two Aryna Sabalenka suffer a heavy defeat to Mirra Andreeva in a match where she won just four games, despite leading 4-1.

While this is a one-sided result, Sabalenka is still some way from having won the fewest amount of games in a WTA Finals match.

Marion Bartoli suffered the heaviest defeat in WTA Finals history in 2007

Marion Bartoli is a former Wimbledon champion and world number seven, but she never actually qualified for the WTA Finals automatically in her career.

Instead, in 2007, the year that Bartoli reached the Wimbledon final for the first time, the Frenchwoman was in Madrid, where the WTA Finals were held that year, as the first alternate. Bartoli was then propelled into the WTA Finals field after Serena Williams withdrew following her first round-robin due to injury.

In Bartoli's opening match, she would face top seed Justine Henin . Henin led the head-to-head against Bartoli, but the latter had won their most recent encounter going into the WTA Finals meeting after stunning the Belgian in the Wimbledon semi-finals earlier that year.

Henin was clearly hungry for revenge and beat Bartoli 6-0, 6-0, inflicting the first 'double bagel' in history at the WTA Finals, which is yet to have been repeated since.

Following this dominant win, Henin admitted that revenge was on her mind, "I wanted to take revenge. Wimbledon is far away now. She was better than me that day and that was it. Now a few months later I'm fresh and in Wimbledon I was pretty tired. I had a pretty good reaction after that defeat though and it helped me."

Although this ended any hopes of Bartoli advancing to the semi-finals, she was able to bounce back and get one round-robin win after her next opponent Jelena Jankovic retired following losing the first set. Bartoli would leave Madrid with mixed results, while Henin went on to win the WTA Finals title unbeaten.

Bartoli would return to the WTA Finals four years later in Istanbul, once again as an alternate after replacing Maria Sharapova . Sharapova had already played two matches before withdrawing due to injury, but Bartoli was able to win her only match against eventual runner-up Victoria Azarenka.

This was the last time Bartoli played at the WTA Finals, having retired from tennis before the event took place in 2013, which was the year that she became a Grand Slam champion after winning Wimbledon.

articles.title: Jessica Pegula wins thrilling contest at WTA Finals, Coco Gauff eliminated
articles.summary: Pegula’s win, in the final group one round-robin match, meant Gauff was knocked out of the season-ending championships.
articles.body:
Jessica Pegula saved a match point en route to a gritty 7-6 (7/2), 4-6, 7-5 win over Linda Noskova on Thursday to advance out of ⁠her round-robin group at the WTA Finals and send fellow American Coco Gauff packing from the season-ending championships.

Pegula had a career-high 16 aces while Wimbledon champion Noskova had a career-high 15 double faults in a see-saw battle that spanned two ⁠hours and 45 minutes at the tournament, which was moved from Riyadh to Indian Wells due to the United States-Israel war on Iran .

“I’ve learned that sometimes the serve feels good and sometimes it doesn’t, and how to manage the days when it doesn’t and to ride it when you are serving well,” Pegula told reporters.

“I don’t think I served that well in my first ‌couple matches and I served great today. Sometimes there’s no rhyme or reason.”

In the end, Noskova, Gauff and Pegula all finished 2-1 in the group while alternate Marta Kostyuk went 0-3.

Noskova went 5-2 in sets to win the group, followed by Pegula at 5-3 and Gauff at 4-3.

The win sets up a first meeting between Pegula and Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva in the semifinals on Saturday.

“It’s the match people wanted; well now you are going to get it,” said Pegula.

Pegula had earlier called Andreeva “ a diva ” who “needs to be humbled”, but didn’t realise that ⁠her remarks were being livestreamed during a practice session before the tournament. In the same ⁠comments, Pegula also praised the World No 3, and she apologised afterwards to those involved.

“She’s fast, she has a great serve, she’s strong, she hits the ball pretty hard, and she’s smart,” Pegula said on Thursday.

Gauff rallies past Kostyuk, but eliminated

Earlier, Gauff rallied to beat ⁠Kostyuk 6-4, 7-5 on a sun-soaked Stadium Two.

After sealing the first set with a stab volley that sent fans leaping to their feet under sunny California desert skies, Gauff ⁠rallied from 1-5 down in the second, winning six games in a row.

“I ⁠was fully prepared to play a third set there,” said Gauff, who needed treatment on her back during the second set.

“It’s the last tournament of the season, so I just wanted to finish it on a high note and give myself the best chance to play the semifinals. Either way, ‌I didn’t want to be sad walking off the court.”

Kostyuk, who won the Madrid title and reached the French Open semifinals , was already eliminated coming into her match against Gauff, having lost to Noskova and Pegula.

Kostyuk, who joined the ‌eight-player ‌tournament as an alternate after top-ranked Elena Rybakina withdrew due to illness, failed to win a set in her three matches as she struggled with a wrist injury.

articles.summary: Sólo Djokovic tiene mejores números en puntos de break a favor y en contra, 'tie breaks' y sets decisivos
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz se ejercita este viernes por tercera vez en las pistas del Inalpi Arena de Turín y lo hace con Flavio Cobolli y bajo la atenta mirada de su técnico Samuel López. El murciano tiene colgado el cartel de favorito en las ATP Finals, a pesar de que Alexander Zverev es el número 1 del y será premiado como el líder del circuito a final de curso. Alcaraz, que viene de ganar los títulos en Viena y en París, está calcando el sprint de Jannik Sinner la pasada campaña. El italiano se impuso en el Open 500 austriaco, posteriormente en el Masters 1000 galo y ganó invicto la cita de maestros. A por ello que va un Carlitos que tiene como arma su juego y cómo se maneja en las situaciones de máxima presión. Según los registros de la ATP, sólo Novak Djokovic tiene mejores actuaciones en situaciones clave de partido como son puntos de break a favor, en contra, tie breaks y sets decisivos. En esa clasificación, Pete Sampras aparece tercero y Rafael Nadal, cuarto. Carlitos decanta a su favor el 42 por ciento de las ocasiones en las que puede romper el servicio del rival. Salva el 64,3 por ciento de puntos de rotura en contra, se lleva el 63,2 por ciento de muertes súbitas, y gana el 72,4 por ciento de partidos en la manga decisiva. Las cifras en positivo del campeón de siete grandes aumentaron en sus dos últimas actuaciones en Viena y en París. Salió airoso de seis de los siete tie breaks disputados. El único que perdió fue con Taylor Fritz en los cuartos del certamen de la capital gala. Precisamente con el estadounidense fue también capaz de derrotarle tras levantar un set y dos pelotas de partido. Alcaraz hace bueno lo de que se juega como se entrena. Y es que en la práctica del jueves con Zverev encadenó seis puntos para ganar el tie break ante la cara de circunstancias de Sascha.

articles.title: Coco Gauff Clears The Air About ‘Stupid’ WTA Finals Rules Complaint After Backlash
articles.summary: Coco Gauff addressed the backlash surrounding her recent comments about the WTA Finals format. Gauff started her run in Indian Wells with a 6-4, 6-7 (5), 6-2...
articles.body:
Coco Gauff addressed the backlash surrounding her recent comments about the WTA Finals format.

Gauff started her run in Indian Wells with a 6-4, 6-7 (5), 6-2 win over compatriot Jessica Pegula. However, she fell in the next round to Linda Noskova, who beat her 6-3, 6-3. The defeat made her advancement in the semifinal round uncertain. Her qualification not only depended on her match against Marta Kostyuk, but also on Pegula's clash against Linda Noskova. After her second loss, Gauff appeared to express frustration with WTA qualification.

Later, following her third-round match against Kostyuk, she was asked to address her previous statement. Gauff clarified that she wasn't calling the format stupid; rather, she meant that thinking about different qualification scenarios while playing a match would be foolish.

"Can I clear that up? Okay. I wasn't saying the format was stupid. I was saying if you get in if you get like in your head while you're playing into all the scenarios that's stupid. But of course, everyone thought I was calling the format [laughter] stupid. But I was trying to because he asked me, 'Am I gonna look at the different scenarios and stuff,' and I was trying to say like no, if I like play while thinking about the scenarios it's stupid because it's tennis. Like you can't, 'Oh, I want to win this match in straight sets.' Every match you want to win in straight sets."

Despite seeing off Marta Kostyuk, Coco Gauff saw her pursuit come to an end as Jessica Pegula finished in second place in Group 1 after dominating Linda Noskova 7-6(2), 4-6, 7-5.

Coco Gauff opens up about the hot mic controversy at the WTA Finals involving her, Mirra Andreeva and Jessica Pegula

Coco Gauff recently opened up about the hot mic incident at the WTA Finals, where Jessica Pegula was heard making statements about her compatriot and Mirra Andreeva. Pegula slammed Andreeva, calling her a 'diva' who 'needed to be humbled.' She also criticized Andreeva's coach, Conchita Martinez, for putting up with her behavior. Pegula also compared Andreeva and Gauff, saying Andreeva could be a better player and surpass Gauff if she had Gauff's mentality. During the event, Gauff addressed the incident, stating that she had no grudges with Pegula.

"Jess, she told me, before I even saw the video, she came and apologized immediately," Gauff said. "Honestly, I didn't really take it. I feel like maybe the other person in the situation got a lot more of it. But she, you know, they both, even her coach, apologized to me. So yeah, I think for me, I'm a competitor, so I'm always going to compete regardless of what's happening off the court. But yeah, I know her heart, and it was all good. I don't feel any type of way."

Jessica Pegula will lock horns with Mirra Andreeva in the semifinals of the WTA Finals.

articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz se ha visto obligado a terminar el entrenamiento con Flavio Cobolli antes de tiempo debido a unas molestias estomacales que arrastraba desde la mañana en el desayuno, según ha podido saber MARCA. El murciano no ha querido forzar la máquina y ha finalizado la sesión preparatoria del viernes 20 minutos antes del horario previsto. Al número tres mundial le rodeaba todo su equipo: Samuel López, Álvaro Alcaraz, Juanjo Moreno, Alberto Lledó y Albert Molina. Carlitos sigue con el estabilizador rotuliano en su rodilla derecha, pero eso no le supone ningún problema en cuanto a movilidad. Lo demostró el jueves en la práctica de máxima intensidad en la que venció a Alexander Zverev, número 1 mundial. El campeón de siete grandes tiene margen suficiente para recuperarse de esos dolores de estómago. Hay tranquilidad en el seno de su equipo. No en vano, tiene programado el partido del debut en las ATP Finals contra Frances Tiafoe el lunes 16, a partir de las 14:00 horas. articles.title: ATP Finals predictions: Sky Sports panel pick their winners and surprise package as Alexander Zverev and Carlos Alcaraz lead the field
articles.summary: Who will win the season-ending tournament in Italy? Are world No 1 Alexander Zverev and No 2 Carlos Alcaraz on collision course? You can watch the Nitto ATP Finals from November 15-22 in Turin on Sky Sports Tennis
articles.body:
Zverev is a two-time champion at the tournament, having lifted the trophy in 2018 and 2021.

The German is in John McEnroe Group with Ben Shelton, Arthur Fils and Rafael Jodar, while Alcaraz - aiming to triumph at the Nitto ATP Finals for the first time - headlines Ivan Lendl Group, which also features Daniil Medvedev, Flavio Cobolli and Frances Tiafoe.

The action takes place at Inalpi Arena from 15-22 November - live on Sky Sports Tennis - but who do Gigi Salmon, Tim Henman and Jamie Murray think will win the tournament? They pick their winners and surprise packages.

Carlos Alcaraz: He is fresh after his lay-off, full of confidence after back-to-back titles, and he really wants this title.

Alexander Zverev: Altitude and his serve will be very difficult to break. Has experience in Turin and winning WTF.

Carlos Alcaraz: I don't think he's played so much tennis this year, and he just won Vienna and Paris. He has never won the Tour finals so that will be a big motivation to get that on his CV.

Carlos Alcaraz: The Spaniard will win because he is the best player on tour right now. He has improved every area of his game on the hard, and that is now translating indoors. With no Jannik Sinner, it's up to him.

Carlos Alcaraz: When he plays the way he plays in Paris indoors, he's pretty much unbeatable. That being said Zverev will try to finish on a good note because he's the No 1 player in the world and has won the tournament before.

Rafael Jodar: He is young with nothing to lose. Just 18 months ago, he was 800 in the world, and now he's a part of the top 10.

He is the quickest player on the ATP Tour to have gone from your debut to the top 10! Beating Gustavo Kuerten by 176 days.

Arthur Fils: The Frenchman loves the big occasion and is so powerful.

Rafael Jodar: People might not think he's a surprise package, but he was the last guy to qualify for the Tour Finals, so he's coming in as the eight-ranked seed, but I'm picking him.

I'd also like to see Arthur Fils do something but the conditions might be too quick for him - just a feeling. But he's got a big game, so let's see.

Frances Tiafoe: He might have been looking pretty tired post US Open but he is a big-match player and can go on a deep run out of nowhere. The vast majority of his points have come from the four big tournaments this year and Turin has everything he needs to be able to turn it on again for a fifth big run of the year.

Speaking at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells, former Australian Open champion Madison Keys told Sky Sports:

"You have Carlos, who won in Paris, and then you have Ben [Shelton], who was in the finals in Paris and US Open.

"I feel like when you have Zverev as the No 1 in the world, you also have Jodar, who is having an incredible year, and Fils, who won Cincinnati in amazing fashion. The difference between all those players is so much closer."

On the American players, Keys said: "I'm cheering for Tiafoe to have an upset, absolutely. But Shelton is also my guy, and he's playing amazing tennis. Everyone is going to play amazing tennis.

articles.summary: El madrileño está disfrutando de la experiencia de estar con los mejores
articles.body: Rafa Jódar ha completado este viernes su segunda sesión de entrenamientos en el Inalpi Arena. El madrileño, que hace su debut en el torneo reservado para los ocho mejores en su primera campaña como profesional, tuvo que madrugar este martes porque tenía la práctica a las 10.00 de la mañana con el esloveno Ziga Sesko. Este se dio a conocer en la presente temporada al ganar el júnior del Open de Australia en individuales y Wimbledon, en dobles. Se convirtió en el primer jugador de su país en conquistar un grande de la categoría. Rafa venía de hacerse la fotografía oficial con el trofeo, junto a los otros sete aspirantes a maestro ATP. La organización eligió para la ocasión la plaza San Carlos. Lucía unas gafas de sol aunque, a diferencia de Frances Tiafoe, no llegó a ponérselas. "Estar aquí no era un objetivo porque es mi primer año en el circuito. Es un honor y un privilegio jugar este torneo con los mejores del mundo", reflexiona el de Leganés. Por su parte, Alexander Zverev, número 1 mundial, reconocía que "Alcaraz ha tenido un regreso excepcional, pero yo me centro en los jugadores que tengo en mi grupo".
